al-magar.name: Al-Magar
al-magar.summary: An advanced Neolithic culture of prehistoric Arabia centered in southwestern Najd, possibly one of the first in the world to widely domesticate animals, especially the horse.

najd.name: Najd
najd.summary: A historical central region of the Arabian Peninsula, home to about a third of Saudi Arabia's population and to the House of Saud.

dilmun.name: Dilmun
dilmun.summary: Ancient civilization in eastern Arabia covering modern Bahrain, Kuwait and eastern Saudi Arabia, a major Bronze Age trading centre between Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley described in Sumerian myth as a paradise.

ubaid-period.name: Ubaid period
ubaid-period.summary: A prehistoric period of Mesopotamia lasting roughly from 6500 to 3800 BC, marking the earliest known settlements on the southern Mesopotamian alluvial plain.

dosariyah.name: Dosariyah
dosariyah.summary: An archaeological site in eastern Saudi Arabia from the late 6th and early 5th millennium BCE, notable for the earliest Ubaid-style pottery found in the country.

hail-province-saudi-arabia.name: Hail Province
hail-province-saudi-arabia.summary: A province in north-central Saudi Arabia's Najd region, named for its capital city and known for its twin mountain ranges and as the homeland of Hatim al-Tai.

rock-art-of-hail-province.name: Rock Art in the Ha'il Region
rock-art-of-hail-province.summary: UNESCO World Heritage site in Saudi Arabia with petroglyphs and inscriptions at two desert locations, holding 8,000 years of history.

al-ula.name: Al-Ula
al-ula.summary: An ancient oasis city in northwest Arabia on the incense trade route, once capital of the Lihyanites and near the Nabataean site of Hegra.

jubbah-saudi-arabia.name: Jubbah
jubbah-saudi-arabia.summary: An oasis city in Saudi Arabia's Ha'il Region, on an old caravan route, known for abundant agriculture and groundwater, and for nearby ancient rock art and lake deposits.

levant.name: The Levant
levant.summary: A subregion of West Asia along the eastern Mediterranean, narrowly covering Syria, Lebanon, Jordan, Israel, Palestine and Cyprus, historically used more broadly for the lands stretching from Greece to Egypt.

african-wild-ass.name: African wild ass
african-wild-ass.summary: A wild desert-dwelling relative of the horse, native to the Horn of Africa and thought to be the ancestor of the domestic donkey; now critically endangered, with about 570 left in the wild.

aurochs.name: Aurochs
aurochs.summary: An extinct wild ancestor of domestic cattle, once found from western Europe to East Asia, with the last known individual dying in the late 17th or early 18th century.
